subject: paediatrics
title: Pediatric Immunodeficiencies: Agammaglobulinemia, SCID, and CGD

steps.tx: Congenital genetic mutations disrupting immune system ontogeny predispose children to recurrent, severe, unusual infections. Warning signs of **pediatric primary immunodeficiency** include eight or more new ear infections within one year, two or more serious sinus infections, persistent oral candidiasis after one year of age, failure to thrive, recurrent deep skin or organ abscesses, two or more episodes of deep-seated sepsis, and family history of early infant death.
steps.say: Primary immunodeficiencies present with recurrent, deep-seated, or opportunistic infections and failure to thrive. Family history of early unexplained infant death is a major clue.

left.title: Jeffrey Modell Warning Signs
points: >=4 new ear infections within 1 year
>=2 serious sinus infections within 1 year
>=2 months on antibiotics with little effect
>=2 pneumonias within 1 year; failure to gain weight

right.title: Microbial Pathogen Associations
points: B-cell / Antibody defects: encapsulated pyogenic bacteria (Pneumococcus)
T-cell defects: viruses, fungi (Candida), Pneumocystis jirovecii
Phagocyte defects: catalase-positive bacteria (Staph aureus), fungi
Complement defects: recurrent Neisseria meningitidis infections

steps.tx: X-linked recessive mutations in the Bruton tyrosine kinase gene abolish B-lymphocyte maturation beyond the pre-B stage. Manifesting in male infants after six months as maternal transplacental IgG wanes, **Bruton X-linked agammaglobulinaemia** (XLA) presents with recurrent sinopulmonary pyogenic bacterial infections (Streptococcus pneumoniae, Haemophilus influenzae). Physical examination demonstrates a striking complete absence of tonsillar lymphoid tissue and peripheral lymph nodes.
steps.say: Bruton agammaglobulinemia affects infant boys as maternal IgG fades after six months. Absence of tonsils and lymph nodes is pathognomonic, with profound pan-hypogammaglobulinemia.

rows: Confirms block in pre-B cell maturation
Prevents bronchiectasis and chronic lung damage

steps.tx: Profound congenital defects in both cellular and humoral immunity constitute the most severe pediatric medical emergency. In infants with **severe combined immunodeficiency** (SCID), mutations in the common gamma chain (IL2RG) or adenosine deaminase (ADA) abolish T-cell development and secondary B-cell function. Infants present under six months with intractable candidiasis, chronic diarrhea, failure to thrive, Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia, and absent thymic shadow.
steps.say: Severe combined immunodeficiency is a pediatric emergency caused by T and B cell defects. Infants under six months present with thrush, chronic diarrhea, and Pneumocystis pneumonia.

vis.alt: Flowchart depicting genetic mutations, absent thymic shadow on chest radiograph, and T-B-NK flow cytometry immunophenotyping in SCID.
vis.caption: Diagnostic flowchart and immunological phenotypes across genetic variants of severe combined immunodeficiency. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: Immediate protective isolation and strict avoidance of live viral or bacterial vaccines prevent fatal disseminated infections. In infants with SCID, **live attenuated vaccine contraindications** are absolute: administering BCG causes disseminated fatal BCGosis, while live oral rotavirus or polio vaccines cause vaccine-strain paralysis. Blood products must be strictly irradiated and cytomegalovirus-negative, and allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation is curative.
steps.say: Live vaccines like BCG and rotavirus are strictly contraindicated in SCID, causing fatal dissemination. All blood products must be irradiated, and stem cell transplant is curative.

left.title: Strict Contraindications in SCID
points: Live vaccines: BCG, Rotavirus, OPV, MMR, Varicella strictly banned
Unirradiated blood transfusions cause fatal graft-versus-host disease
Exposure to cytomegalovirus (CMV)-positive blood products
Delayed referral for stem cell transplantation

right.title: Immediate Prophylaxis Protocol
points: Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole for Pneumocystis jirovecii
Oral fluconazole for systemic Candida prevention
Intravenous or subcutaneous replacement immunoglobulin
Allogeneic HSCT within 3 months achieves >90% cure

steps.tx: Defective nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide phosphate oxidase enzyme complexes abolish phagocytic generation of superoxide radicals. Inherited predominantly as an X-linked recessive defect in the CYBB gene encoding gp91phox, **pediatric chronic granulomatous disease** (CGD) leaves phagocytes capable of engulfing pathogens but incapable of producing oxidative respiratory burst. Patients suffer recurrent granulomatous abscesses caused by catalase-positive bacteria and fungi.
steps.say: Chronic granulomatous disease impairs phagocytic respiratory burst due to NADPH oxidase defects. Children suffer recurrent abscesses from catalase-positive organisms like Staph and Aspergillus.

rows: Frequent cause of occult bone infection

steps.tx: Laboratory evaluation of neutrophil respiratory burst activity confirms the functional defect in oxidative radical production. Historically assessed using the **nitroblue tetrazolium reduction test** (NBT test), normal phagocytes reduce yellow soluble NBT into insoluble blue-black formazan crystals, whereas CGD neutrophils fail to produce color. Modern diagnosis utilizes dihydrorhodamine-123 (DHR) flow cytometry, which measures fluorescence shift following phorbol myristate acetate stimulation.
steps.say: The nitroblue tetrazolium test shows failure to reduce dye to blue formazan. Modern dihydrorhodamine flow cytometry demonstrates absent oxidative burst fluorescence.

left.title: Nitroblue Tetrazolium (NBT) Test
points: Normal neutrophils reduce yellow NBT to blue formazan crystals
CGD neutrophils show 0% reduction (remain clear/yellow)
Qualitative, observer-dependent microscopic test
Useful historical screening assay

right.title: Dihydrorhodamine (DHR) Flow Cytometry
points: Measures non-fluorescent DHR oxidation to green rhodamine-123
Phorbol myristate acetate (PMA) stimulates neutrophils
Complete absence of fluorescent shift confirms CGD
Identifies X-linked carrier mothers (bimodal peak)

steps.tx: An X-linked recessive triad of microthrombocytopenia, severe eczema, and progressive combined immunodeficiency characterizes actin cytoskeletal remodeling defects. Arising from mutations in the WAS gene encoding the Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome protein, **Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome in boys** manifests in early infancy with petechiae, bloody diarrhea, intractable flexural atopic eczema, and recurrent encapsulated infections. The pathognomonic finding is microthrombocytes with small platelet volume.
steps.say: Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome is an X-linked triad of thrombocytopenia with tiny microplatelets, severe eczema, and recurrent infections. Platelet volume is characteristically small.

rows: Low platelets (<50,000) with low MPV (<5 fL)
Severe flexural and facial eczematous dermatitis
Low IgM, elevated IgA and IgE, declining T-cells

steps.tx: Microscopic evaluation of peripheral platelets distinguishes Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome from immune thrombocytopenic purpura definitively. While idiopathic immune thrombocytopenia displays large giant platelets (elevated mean platelet volume MPV), Wiskott-Aldrich is uniquely characterized by **microthrombocytes with low MPV**, measuring five femtolitres or less. Prophylactic trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, intravenous immunoglobulin, and early allogeneic stem cell transplantation are mandatory.
steps.say: Wiskott-Aldrich platelets are uniquely tiny with a low mean platelet volume, distinguishing it from ITP where platelets are enlarged. Stem cell transplantation is curative.

left.title: Wiskott-Aldrich Syndrome (WAS)
points: Microthrombocytes: small platelet size (MPV <5 fL)
Persistent congenital thrombocytopenia from birth
Elevated serum IgA and IgE; low serum IgM
High risk of lymphoma and autoimmune cytopenias

right.title: Immune Thrombocytopenic Purpura (ITP)
points: Megathrombocytes: large platelet size (MPV >11 fL)
Acute sudden post-viral onset in healthy toddler
Normal immunoglobulin concentrations (IgG, IgA, IgM)
Excellent spontaneous recovery rate (>80%)
